newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel slightly higher against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel slightly higher against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar on Wednesday in trendless trading, dealers said.

"The market continues to be very quiet with the shekel trading in a narrow range. Despite that the Bank of Israel had to intervene (by buying dollars) on a moderate scale to support the basket," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the foreign currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3650 shekels against 3.3670 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6541 shekels against 3.6536 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7323 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7405 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.9986 shekels after 1.9967 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3630 shekels.
